steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Embellishment adds surface detail: beading, sequins, embroidery, quilting — each creates different textural and visual effects. | Key Fact: Felting mats fibres together: wet felting uses soap, water and friction; needle felting uses barbed needles to interlock fibres. | Key Fact: Heat manipulation of synthetic fabrics can create permanent sculptural forms — crumpling, pleating, melting. | Key Fact: Mixed media textiles break boundaries by incorporating non-traditional materials: paper, wire, plastic, found objects.
